reason: Flusher processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:53,105), i.e. `SpawnProcess`, which subclasses `BaseProcess` and not `multiprocessing.Process`, so the `isinstance` guard at flusher.py:346-347 is always False and `terminate()` is never called in `join()`. Processes only stop if they honour the `stopped` flag (not checked by running code; the `isinstance` result rests on CPython's class hierarchy), and the same guard already existed before the patch, which rewrote these lines into the per-process loop.
